flagged.evidence: The scope's A-page manifest assigns this lemma among 49 items, but library/scheme-theory/blowups-exceptional-divisors-and-strict-transforms.md lists 48 and omits it. Searching current library Markdown found no placement. The point-pushforward and projection-formula items depend on this unhomed supplier.

The page says the exceptional curve has 'conormal sheaf of degree $-1$'. The current lem-exceptional-curve-normal-bundle-minus-one, Statement and step 2.1, gives conormal O(1), degree +1, and normal O(-1), degree -1. [Stacks Lemma 54.3.1(3)](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0AGP) corroborates these signs.

The page describes the assigned rational-map example as P^1 dashrightarrow P^1. The current ex-blowup-rational-map-p1 instead defines A^2_k dashrightarrow P^1_k by [x:y] off the origin and resolves it by Bl_0 A^2_k. The summarized source scheme is incorrect.

The summary characterizes its counterexample as 'blowing up a singular centre'. The current cex-blowup-singular-center-not-smooth explicitly states: 'The point center Spec k is abstractly regular; the immersion into the singular ambient scheme is not regular.' Its witness concerns a singular ambient surface, not a singular center.

The remark says exceptional intersection points are determined by 'the linear factors of the leading form', without a splitting-field hypothesis. Take k=R and f=x^2+y^2, a reduced equation of multiplicity two. Its leading form has no real linear factor, but the first strict-transform chart has equation 1+s^2=0 and intersects E in Spec R[s]/(1+s^2), a nonempty closed point of degree two. Over the stated arbitrary field, irreducible homogeneous factors determine the closed points.

The Statement concludes 'and W′ is not a single dominant component'. Take X=A^2_k, I=(x,y), and W=X. Its strict transform is the entire integral blowup, hence a single irreducible component dominating W. The proof establishes preservation of finite scheme-theoretic unions, not unconditional nonsingleness of the strict transform.

The bullet asserts that a closed point center on a regular surface has exceptional P^1 over its residue field. Its cited theorem assumes a regular finite-type k-scheme of pure dimension two. Without finite type or dim O_{S,p}=2, take p=(x), q=(x-1,y), T=k[x,y]\(p union q), and S=Spec T^{-1}k[x,y]. This is a regular Noetherian integral surface of dimension two, but p becomes a closed point with one-dimensional DVR local ring. Its ideal (x) is effective Cartier, so its blowup is the identity and its exceptional fiber is Spec k(y), not P^1_{k(y)}.

The on-disk locator cites 'Lemmas 10.70.2 ... and 10.70.5, the incidence algebra of a regular sequence'. [Section 10.70](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/052P) has Example 10.70.5, whose hypothesis is a polynomial algebra P=R[t_1,...,t_n] with its variable ideal. It gives an affine-chart presentation, not the asserted arbitrary-regular-sequence incidence-algebra result. The item's local proof supplies that result, but this source locator misidentifies both the entry and its scope.

The on-disk locator says 'Definition 10.70.1 and the Veronese discussion following it'. The complete mathematical text of [Section 10.70](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/052P), Definition 10.70.1 through Lemma 10.70.12, contains no Veronese discussion. The actual power-invariance proof uses the opened local supplier lem-proj-veronese-invariance; the claimed external locator does not exist.
